The grid has $(d+1)^2$ vertices, of which the two rough sides contain $2(d+1)$ distinct vertices; hence $Q_0$ has $(d-1)(d+1)=d^2-1$ coordinates. There are $d^2$ faces. [F1, given, algebra]
source_lines.86: 1.2 The columns of $\partial_2$ are independent. If a face combination $b\in Q_2$ has zero boundary, its coefficient on each top horizontal physical edge is the coefficient of the unique face immediately below that edge, so all top-row face coefficients vanish. On the next horizontal row, each boundary coefficient is the sum of the face coefficients immediately above and below; the already-zero top row forces the next row to vanish. Repeating downward gives $b=0$. Hence $\operatorname{rank}\partial_2=d^2$. [F1, given, algebra]
source_lines.88: 1.3 A self-avoiding left-to-right path starts with one of the $d+1$ horizontal edges from a left rough vertex into the patch. At each subsequent vertex the square grid has at most four incident edges, and the edge just used cannot be immediately traversed backwards, leaving at most three choices. Thus for length $\ell\ge1$ there are at most $(d+1)3^{\ell-1}\le(d+1)3^\ell$ such paths. [F1, algebra]
source_lines.98: 5.1 For a relative cycle $z$, let $q_i(z)$ be the parity of its selected horizontal edges between columns $i$ and $i+1$, for $i=0,\ldots,d-1$. Summing the relative vertex-boundary equations over columns $1,\ldots,i$ cancels every interior edge twice and leaves only the two cut sets, so $q_0(z)=q_i(z)$. Each face boundary has either zero or two horizontal edges in a given column strip, so $q_i$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}\partial_2$. The straight horizontal row $z_0$ has $q_i(z_0)=1$ for every $i$, and is therefore not a relative boundary. Since the quotient in step 4.2 is one-dimensional, every nonzero Z logical class has all $q_i=1$; it must contain at least one horizontal edge in each of the $d$ disjoint strips. Thus its weight is at least $d$, and $z_0$ attains $d$. [F1, F3, step 4.2, algebra]
source_lines.100: 6.1 In the edge subgraph of a relative cycle, every vertex outside $R$ has even degree, so all odd-degree vertices lie in $R$. The handshake identity $\sum_v\deg(v)=2|E|$ shows there are an even number of them. Add one dummy vertex joined to each odd boundary vertex; every degree in the augmented finite graph is now even. Starting with any unused edge, follow unused edges: at a vertex other than the start, the number of used incident edges is odd, so its even total degree leaves an unused edge. Finiteness therefore closes the trail at its start. Removing this closed trail preserves even degrees; repeating decomposes all edges into closed trails. Deleting dummy edges leaves cycles and paths with endpoints in $R$. Across any vertical cut, a cycle crosses evenly and a path crosses oddly exactly when its endpoints lie on opposite sides. Since $q_i=1$, at least one path joins the left and right rough sides. Removing repeated-vertex loops leaves a self-avoiding such path contained in the support. It crosses each of the $d$ disjoint vertical cuts, so its length is at least $d$. [step 5.1, construct, algebra]
source_lines.102: 6.2 For X-type supports, use the dual graph with one vertex per face and top and bottom exterior vertices, and one dual edge crossing each physical primal edge. The normalizer condition makes each face vertex even-degree, and X checks are the dual boundaries around vertices outside $R$. Their quotient has dimension $\dim(C_1/C_2)=1$ by step 4.1. A straight dual path from top to bottom is in the normalizer because it enters and leaves each face, and it crosses the straight Z logical row once. Since that Z cycle commutes with every X check, this odd intersection shows the dual path is not an X check; it represents the nonzero class. [F1, F2, F3, F6, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 5.1, algebra]
source_lines.104: 7.1 For an X support $x$, let $q'_j(x)$ be the parity of selected horizontal primal edges in row $j$, for $j=0,\ldots,d$. Each X stabilizer has either zero or two such edges in each row, so every $q'_j$ vanishes on the X stabilizer space. The straight dual path from step 6.2 has $q'_j=1$ for all $j$. Since the X logical quotient is one-dimensional, every nontrivial class has $q'_j=1$ in each of the $d+1$ disjoint rows. Its weight is therefore at least $d+1$. In the dual support graph every face vertex has even degree, so the finite even-degree decomposition from the path argument in step 6.1, now with top and bottom exterior vertices as boundary vertices, splits it into cycles and paths ending at those exterior vertices. A cycle and a path with both endpoints at the same exterior vertex cross each horizontal cut evenly; since every $q'_j=1$, at least one path joins top to bottom. Every such path has length at least $d+1$, and the straight dual path attains this bound. [F1, F3, step 6.1, step 6.2, algebra]

concrete_diagram_content: Draw wires A,B,C in that order, with |psi> on A and |Phi+> shared across B,C; put CNOT A->B before H on A (the rightmost gate in V_AB acts first); label the four output branches ab on A,B and X^b Z^a on C. Do not imply measurement is part of V_AB, which is only the encoding unitary.
